analysis.title: Pinterest Inc. (PINS) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Strategic Priorities & Investment Areas Remain in Focus Against Near-Term Growth Headwinds
key_insights: GS maintains Buy on PINS and cuts the 12-month price target to $26 from $30 (price $19.92, 30.5% upside), lowering forward operating estimates after a Q3 miss and a below-consensus Q4 guide.
Q3'26 revenue was $1,174mm, 3% below both GS ($1,205mm) and consensus ($1,205mm), and below the $1,190-1,210mm guidance range. Revenue grew 12% y/y.

Europe drove the miss: Q3 Europe revenue was $193mm, 11% below GS and 8% below consensus, flat y/y. Management cited a larger-than-expected impact from EU de minimis changes, timing around major global events, and no FX tailwind.

Q4'26 guidance for revenue ($1.425-1.475bn) and Adj. EBITDA ($538-588mm) is below GS and Street estimates. Management expects EU regulatory pressure to persist into Q4 with early signs of stabilization.
Q3 MAUs reached a record 661mm, above GS (649mm) and consensus (655mm), up 10% y/y. Searches, boards created and outbound clicks in UCAN all grew faster than users.
User behavior increasingly shows commercial intent: more than half of searches are commercial, and Pinterest Assistant usage skews more heavily to 80%.

UCAN revenue has reaccelerated to a mid-teens growth rate YTD, driven by better performance advertising, measurement and go-to-market execution. Management sees UCAN as proof the monetization playbook works and is applying it internationally.

AI initiatives are gaining traction: 70% of search journeys start with AI-powered recommendations, advertiser adoption of AI tools is rising, and the open model strategy is producing internal efficiency gains.
Management acknowledged that closing the international monetization gap is a key opportunity but will take time.

GS cuts Q4'26 revenue to $1.47bn from $1.53bn, Adj. EBITDA to $581mm from $633mm and GAAP EPS to $0.43 from $0.51. For 2027 it cuts revenue to $5.48bn from $5.53bn, Adj. EBITDA to $1.75bn from $1.78bn and GAAP EPS to $0.74 from $0.87.
The biggest estimate cut is Europe revenue: Q4'26 down 21% to $222mm, 2026 down 9%, 2027 down 14% and 2028 down 16%.

Price target is an equal blend of 2.5x EV/Sales (from 3.0x) on NTM+1 year estimates and 18.5x EV/GAAP EBITDA (unchanged) on NTM+4 year estimates discounted back 3 years at 12%. Scenario values are $15 downside, $26 base and $40 upside.
Long-term, GS expects steady mid-teens+ % compounded revenue growth and margin expansion, anchored on shoppable content, direct response/bottom-funnel ad budgets and partnerships.
GS expects investor debate to center on the trajectory of topline growth over the near-to-medium term amid international headwinds and the re-positioning of go-to-market and execution.

market_movers.rationale: Buy maintained and PT cut to $26 from $30 on lower forward estimates after the Q3 revenue miss and below-consensus Q4 guide, driven by EU de minimis headwinds. Implies 30.5% upside from $19.92.

sector_views.rationale: The report covers one company, so it states no sector stance. It describes ad-budget and macro headwinds as a risk to PINS and sees direct response and bottom-funnel budgets as a long-term growth driver.

earnings_insights: PINS Q3'26 reported revenue $1,174mm vs GS est $1,205mm and consensus $1,205mm (guidance $1,190-1,210mm), +12% y/y.
PINS Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA $339mm vs GS est $352mm and consensus $349mm (guidance $335-355mm), margin 28.9%.
PINS Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS $0.04 vs GS est $0.06 and consensus $0.09. Reported GAAP EBITDA was $41mm vs GS est $53mm and consensus $74mm.
PINS Q3'26 reported regional revenue: US & Canada $894mm (+14% y/y, 1% below GS), Europe $193mm (0% y/y, 11% below GS), Rest of World $87mm (+24% y/y, 3% below GS).
PINS Q4'26 company guidance: revenue $1.425-1.475bn and Adj. EBITDA $538-588mm, both below GS and Street estimates.

GS new estimates (not reported): Q4'26 revenue $1.466bn, Adj. EBITDA $581mm, GAAP EPS $0.43, Adj. EPS $0.78. FY26E revenue $4.827bn, Adj. EBITDA $1.438bn, Adj. EPS $1.94. FY27E revenue $5.478bn, Adj. EBITDA $1.746bn, Adj. EPS $2.33.
GS estimate changes for Adj. EPS: FY26E to $1.94 from $2.02, FY27E to $2.33 from $2.45, FY28E to $2.75 from $2.83.

macro_indicators.reading: Larger-than-anticipated headwind to PINS European revenue, expected to persist into Q4 with early signs of stabilization
macro_indicators.interpretation: EU regulatory changes pressure ad spend from cross-border e-commerce advertisers and weigh on PINS European monetization.

risk_factors: Macroeconomic headwinds that persist or are more severe than expected, weighing on ad spend budgets over the next several quarters.
MAU growth fails to stabilize or keeps trending lower post-pandemic.
International monetization deviates from expectations in timing and magnitude (competition, macro and geopolitical risks to ad spend, international sales force execution).
Execution risk on the shopping and full-funnel commerce opportunity from competition, weak advertiser or user adoption of social commerce, or internal execution.
Increased regulatory scrutiny of media and eCommerce platforms over user data and privacy.
Volatility from the global macro environment and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.

tension_points.bull_case: Record 661mm MAUs, UCAN revenue back to mid-teens growth YTD, rising AI tool adoption and a shift to commercial search intent support steady mid-teens+ % compounded revenue growth and margin expansion long-term.
tension_points.bear_case: Q3 revenue missed and Q4 was guided below Street on larger EU de minimis headwinds, and management says closing the international monetization gap will take time.
tension_points.what_invalidates: MAU growth fails to stabilize, international monetization deviates from expectations in timing or magnitude, or macro headwinds weigh on ad budgets over the next several quarters.

theme_stances.key_argument: Despite near-term EU headwinds, user growth, UCAN reacceleration and AI traction support mid-teens+ compounded revenue growth over the long term.
theme_stances.evidence: steady ~mid-teens+ % compounded revenue growth and margin expansion
